artifacts.summary: Traces <leader>as to the sf1 terminal integration and establishes that no change confined to this repository can durably add the requested message-part dividers, because sf1's rendering lives entirely in an untracked, auto-updating vendor payload (~/.sapience/sf1.py) outside any repo this agent system manages; lays out three concrete paths (disposable vendor hand-edit, a PTY-proxy wrapper owned by this repo, or a reapply-at-activation patch sited in ~/.dotfiles/packages/sapience-flake) with their durability/risk tradeoffs.

memory_candidates.content: In this nvim config repo, every terminal-embedded AI chat integration (sf1/Sapience, Claude Code, OpenCode) follows the same shape: a snacks.terminal window whose Lua code (position/size/visibility only) never touches the running program's output bytes. Any request to restyle message content/spacing inside one of these chat panes cannot be satisfied by editing the nvim config alone -- the fix has to live in the external binary itself or in a PTY-proxying wrapper that intercepts its output stream.

~/.sapience/*.py (including sf1.py, mcp.py, sapience_cli.py etc.) is vendor payload: not a git repo, fetched by curl from app.spnc.ai, and silently overwritten by a daily auto-update (~/.sapience/update.log shows auto-update: updated/current entries roughly once per day, with per-file timestamped backups). ~/.dotfiles/packages/sapience-flake/flake.nix documents this is deliberate (no Nix derivation, because a pinned fetchurl would fight the vendor's own self-updater). Any local hand-edit to these files should be treated as disposable, not durable.

user_decision.question: Task 608 asks to add blank-line/divider styling between message parts in the <leader>as (sf1) chat pane. Research found this cannot be done durably by editing anything inside /home/benjamin/.config/nvim: sf1's rendering lives entirely in ~/.sapience/sf1.py, an untracked vendor payload that a daily auto-update can silently overwrite. Which path should the plan phase pursue?
options: Option A -- Hand-edit ~/.sapience/sf1.py directly (3 one-line insertions at known boundaries), accepted as a disposable local patch that may be silently lost on the next vendor auto-update

Option B -- Build a PTY-proxying wrapper inside this repo (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/sapience/), invoked in place of the bare "sf1" command, that rewrites the output stream to insert blank lines by pattern-matching sf1's known prompt/banner/sources-line text
Option C -- Abandon or redirect this task; file a new task in ~/.dotfiles (the repo that owns the sapience-flake packaging) to reapply the same patch idempotently at every `sapience update`
user_decision.recommended: Option B -- Build a PTY-proxying wrapper inside this repo (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/sapience/), invoked in place of the bare "sf1" command, that rewrites the output stream to insert blank lines by pattern-matching sf1's known prompt/banner/sources-line text
user_decision.obligation: The chosen option must durably satisfy the task's styling goal without requiring an edit outside /home/benjamin/.config/nvim's own task-management scope (per .claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md's task-siting rule) and without silently losing the fix to the vendor's daily auto-update cycle documented in ~/.sapience/update.log.
